findings.claim: The worst-case false-pass rate W9 and the charge c9 were only measured at a candidate pool of 300 a session. At the lane's own pool sizes the cell this file binds on (an adversarial 'low-volatility names win' prior) is above the goal's 15% per run. Even at pool 300, a second fresh replicate puts c9 at 0.14, not 0.13. Every calib_w9 fresh and binding cell uses nbar 300. The live pools are about 420-850 candidates a session for EVL-WL-ON and 340-620 for EVL-WL-O1 before merging by issuer (section 16; PREREG-EVL-7's table, whose calibration binds at nbar 300 and 800). The fixer's selection re-ran only cells within 4 points of the search maximum, capped at 6, so the pool-600 cells were never re-run on fresh seeds. Their search reads were ON 0.110 and O1 0.100 at 200 programs each. History adds more than section 11.2 states: +0.023 (noise history) to +0.058 (adversarial prior) over the cold learner at pool 600, against the +0.016 to +0.027 stated.

findings.claim: W1 is not applied to PREREG-EVL-7's newest text, which changed after this file was written. EVL-7's text sha256 2f2cff59 (written 17:26Z, its final fix round from 17:05Z) DELETES ln(adv20/1e7) and ln(prev_close/20) from its cold learners. When those levels are built from the issuer's own prices they encode the persistent issuer effect. This file's section 4 keeps both in item 7 and says item 7 is 'what PREREG-EVL-7's newest text keeps' (it cites 3b0b6b87, superseded). calib_w9 also draws both levels as the lens's static values, never built from the issuer's own returns, so W9 omits a channel EVL-7 measured. EVL-7's text now states 'One accounting holds for PREREG-EVL-6, this file and PREREG-EVL-9: a pass on a persistent issuer effect is a false pass.'
findings.evidence: evl7/PREREG-EVL-7.md (sha256 2f2cff59cc4c3032a7828a95b7096eec5bb9577a14d0d67c94ce3ed260d2da9), section 1.4 items 10-11 and section 5.2(2). It states 0.1280 (SE 0.0106) with own-price levels against 0.0830 with static levels for EVL-LRN-O1 at pool 300, and picks' issuer effect +25.1 bp against +2.1 bp. findings.fix: Section 4: delete item 7's ln(adv20/1e7) and ln(prev_close/20), as PREREG-EVL-7's items 10-11 do. That gives 54 columns (EVL-WL-O1) and 56 (EVL-WL-ON), or 53 under the dmove condition. adv20 is still read by the cost, the tiebreak and the benchmark split, never as a column. Cite EVL-7's sha256 2f2cff59 and re-read its frozen text at the freeze. findings.claim: The warm close part is not aligned with PREREG-EVL-7's newest receipts, and EVL-WL-ON's one own-return column would read missing live. PREREG-EVL-7 now runs its learner part as its OWN receipt, decide-open-lrnlive:<D> / decide-close-lrnlive:<D>. It starts after the House's decide-* receipt finishes and fetches the '1530' marks of the pool's candidates as its own first read. This file (sections 2.1 and 7.3, timing9) starts decide-close-warm9 on the lane's decide-close receipt and assumes EVL-7's part, inside that receipt, has already stored the marks. So the warm part typically runs before the marks exist, and every candidate reads dmove_missing 1 live. The history always has dmove. That is a systematic train/serve skew on the one own-return column, and section 7.3's timing table is stale. W11 also requires the warm part to run after every earlier file's rows, and EVL-7's lrnlive is such a row. EVL-7's A113 rule for real money is not mirrored either: a learner pick waits for its own receipt and keeps no room from earlier rows while it waits.
findings.evidence: evl7/PREREG-EVL-7.md (2f2cff59) section 1.7 'ISOLATION, ITS OWN LIVE RECEIPT', lines 299-312; real-money rule lines 355-362; item 15 lines 252-253 ('fetched by the learner's own live part at or after tau'). EVL-9 section 2.1 lines 231-238 and section 7.3 table rows 766-768.
findings.fix:
(a) decide-open-warm9 and decide-close-warm9 start on the finish (any status, or its bound) of EVL-7's decide-*-lrnlive:<D> and of PREREG-EVL-8's part, whichever is later.
(b) dmove reads marks with fetched_at <= marks_read_at, as now. When EVL-7's part stored none, the candidate reads dmove_missing 1, and the report counts that share per close.
(c) Re-run timing9.py on EVL-7's newest bounds (90 s / 120 s from its own start, less EVL5_FINISH) and restate when real money can buy at the close.
(d) Adopt EVL-7's A113 waiting rule word for word for this file's picks.
(e) Add a B6 test: a live ON decision whose candidates have stored marks reads them.

findings.claim:
The abandon option is not fully closed, contrary to section 1.2's claim that 'a VOID ... carries no option on an outcome'.
(1) VOID (iii), no TRAIN-START by the 5th session after CODE_PIN_9, is free, and it is reached by a person's inaction: the captain starts the job.
(2) The captain also runs B7's export with a free --sessions range. Fewer than 3 overlap sessions for a pool's first program fails G2, which is a free VOID (i).
(3) Anyone can rebuild the model before TRAIN-START. The pinned code is public on prereg/evl-9 at CODE_PIN_9, the sources are public SEC and Alpaca data, and training is deterministic. The would-be learner's picks over the Oct 19 to CODE_PIN_9 sessions can then be scored against House outcomes, and the version voided at no cost, any number of times.
(4) blake-desktop gives the operator account passwordless sudo, so ltcm-warm's mode 0700 and the private tmpfs are policy, not access control. After TRAIN-START a G4/G5 failure is still a free VOID (section 1.2 (ii)). That contradicts section 0's 'From the moment training starts the version cannot be VOID'.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9 section 1.1 step 3 ('started by the captain'), section 1.2 bullets 1-3, section 6.1 G2 (1), B7 ('--sessions <first>..<last>'), section 0 bullet 2; ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ('Passwordless sudo is enabled').
findings.fix:
Section 1.2:
- From CODE_PIN_9 the job's unit starts by its own timer at the first close after the tag, with no person's step. It runs B7's export itself over every lane session from 2026-10-19 through the last whose decisions finished before the export.
- The reserved 2 x c9 is released ONLY by a G1-G3/G2b failure recorded in a receipt the job pushes itself.
- No TRAIN-START by the 5th session's close: the 2 x c9 is DRAWN.
- After TRAIN-START every outcome, G4 and G5 included, draws it.
- Section 0's sentence is then true as written.
Section 1.4 and section 12 state that sudo exists on the desktop, and that the public code and sources let anyone rebuild the model before T_M, which is why every path after CODE_PIN_9 is charged.

findings.claim: The history set has no cell in which HISTORY carries the issuers' own persistent effect through the columns W1 keeps (the static levels, ln sig20, sector) and g. TAUH covers only dmove's population slope. If the effect partly persists from 2022-2026 into the live window, EVL-WL-O1 reads above its stated worst. The registered tree adds little: its rule checks the 200-issuer minimum only for the best split, and on static columns that often stops it at the root. The channel is the ridge's static projection, which finding 2's deletion mostly removes.

findings.claim: W6 is past-only for the scores but not for their hyperparameter. R* is chosen by fitting on the first 80% of sessions and scoring the last 20% (2025-2026). That R* is then used by every forward-chained fold, so 2023-2025's g_oof uses a rounds count chosen on later years. That inflates the prior's weight on g, which W6 meant to stop; it is a power matter.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9 section 5.1, bullets 'Rounds R*' and 'CROSS-FIT, FORWARD-CHAINED'.
findings.fix: Section 5.1: each fold's tree takes its own R*, chosen on the last 20% of that fold's own training sessions (2023's fold on 2022 alone), and G_full uses the full-window R*. Nobody reads any R*.

findings.claim:
The forward-row entry rule cannot be read the same way live and in a recompute.
- Section 7.2 admits warm_stats rows whose settled_by is before tau, and says 'a row's write time never decides whether it enters'.
- Section 7.1 writes a row only at the first nightly run at which every pool outcome of s is terminal or 2 sessions have passed since s's planned exit. The exit ladder can hold an outcome pending for up to 20 sessions.
- So a row held back by one pending outcome has settled_by before decisions that ran before the row existed. The live decision cannot read it; the catch-up, the recompute and section 7.6 item 1's identity test can.
- The nightly recompute then alarms and holds real money (section 7.5) on an artefact.
findings.evidence: PREREG-EVL-9 section 7.1 first bullet, section 7.2 first bullet, section 7.4 recompute, section 7.6 item 1; section 3.6 exit ladder (sessions 6-20).
findings.fix: Section 7.1 records each row's DUE_AT: the start of the nightly run at which 7.1's rule writes it, a function of outcome statuses as stored each night. Section 7.2 admits rows with due_at before tau, and reports settled_by without using it for entry. Section 7.6's identity test keeps rows by due_at.

findings.claim:
Wording that overstates.
- Section 3.4 and section 0: W7's gap 'changes power only'. The history universe also sets the prior's direction, including the survivors S1's spells add. Its false-pass effect is bounded only by the ADV cells.
- Section 11.2: 'every figure stays at or under PREREG-EVL-6's own 0.13' and 'History does not otherwise raise the rate' fail at the lane's pool sizes (finding 1).
- Section 0's 'From the moment training starts the version cannot be VOID' contradicts section 1.2 (ii) (finding 4).
findings.fix: Reword: 'changes power and the prior's direction, whose false-pass effect is bounded by the ADV cells of section 11.2'. Restate section 11.2's summary lines from the re-measured binding set. Align section 0 with section 1.2 after finding 4's fix.
